question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Operating expenses (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: Recent GAAP opex guides: Q1 FY27 7.7, Q2 8.5, Q3 9.2. Each guide sat ~0.8-0.9B above the prior actual (Q1 7.62, Q2 8.41). Q4 guides historically step up more (+12-15% over the Q3 actual in FY25 and FY26). Management guided FY27 opex growth in the 'low 50s' %. On a FY26 GAAP base of 23.08B with Q1-Q3 at ~25.2B, that implies Q4 of 9.4-10.3B (~9.9 at 52%). On the new non-GAAP basis (includes SBC) the implied Q4 GAAP is ~10.2. Median ~10.0. Market check: searched Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi, no market found.

- Earlier guides: Q4 FY26 guide GAAP ~6.7B vs Q3 FY26 actual ~5.84B (+15%); Q4 FY25 guide ~4.8B vs Q3 FY25 actual ~4.29B (+12%).
- Q2 FY27 call (Aug 2026, Yahoo highlights): FY27 opex expected to grow in the 'low 50s' % (broader portfolio, AI tools usage); q/q growth from compute infrastructure plus compensation. Unclear whether that basis is GAAP or new non-GAAP.
- Implied arithmetic: low-50s on GAAP base 23.08 -> FY27 34.6-35.5B; minus Q1+Q2+Q3guide (~25.2) -> Q4 9.4-10.3B. On a recast non-GAAP-incl-SBC base (~22.8) -> Q4 non-GAAP ~9.9-10.1, GAAP ~+0.2.
- Status quo: NVIDIA always gives 'approximately $X billion' GAAP opex guidance (single figure).

Management has raised the opex outlook before (upper 40s, then low 50s). Actuals land ~0.1B under guide, which pushes up the remainder for Q4. Median 10.1. calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on all actuals and guides (Q1 7.621, Q2 8.408 GAAP; Q3 guide 9.2/9.0; FY26 GAAP 23.076B) and on the 'low 50s' FY growth comment. The one material dispute is factual: whether 'low 50s' is on the GAAP basis or on the restated non-GAAP basis that includes SBC. Without web access I could not settle it, so the distribution covers both readings (~9.85 vs ~10.25). Run 3 leaned toward the non-GAAP basis, Runs 1-2 toward a blend. I added a small upward tilt for management's habit of raising its opex outlook and for Q4 steps being larger. I kept the runs' reference class. The upper escape above 11.25 is negligible; there is a small lower escape (2%) for a sharp cut in hiring or compute spending.
